## Overview

**In plain terms.** Among the children who could not read any nonwords at the start of
the study, *when* did they first come off that floor, and what predicted it? Rather than
the single first-window off-floor transition (the LRPITT11 floor rule), this model uses
all four waves: a discrete-time survival model for the time to first come off the nonword
floor, with the intervention entering as a shift in the hazard of coming off.

**Estimand and design.** The at-risk set is the children at the nonword floor at t1. The
outcome is the interval (t1→t2, t2→t3, t3→t4) in which a child first scores above zero.
The hazard carries a per-interval baseline, the *baseline* (t1) letter-sound knowledge,
word reading and age as prognostic covariates, and a treatment hazard contrast fitted **in
the randomised first interval only**: after the waitlist crossover every person-period row
is treatment-on, so the later intervals carry no arm contrast and fit their own
(both-arms-treated) baseline hazards. `G = 2 − group`, so a positive `tau` means the
intervention arm has the higher first-interval off-floor hazard.

**This is prognostic, not causal.** `tau` is anchored on the randomised first interval
among children at the floor at t1 (a pre-randomisation subgroup), adjusted for the
baseline covariates — a description of who comes off the floor and when, not a licence to
gate-keep, and reported as a prognostic association rather than a causal effect of record.
Floor status mostly reflects incomplete letter-sound foundations (the outcome the
intervention moves most), pointing to continue-and-extend. See the descriptive companion
note and `METHODS.md`.

## Model

With interval baseline hazard $\alpha_k$, treatment-on indicator $\text{trt}_{ik}$, and
standardised baseline covariates $L_{0,i}$ (letter sounds), $W_{0,i}$ (word reading) and
$A_{0,i}$ (age), the discrete-time hazard of coming off the floor uses a
complementary-log-log link:

$$
\text{cloglog}\big(h_{ik}\big) = \alpha_k + \tau\,\text{trt}_{ik}\,[k = 1]
  + \beta_L\,L_{0,i} + \beta_W\,W_{0,i} + \beta_A\,A_{0,i},
\qquad [\,\text{off floor in interval } k\,]_{ik} \sim \text{Bernoulli}(h_{ik}).
$$

The $[k = 1]$ indicator restricts `tau` to the randomised first interval
(`treatment_window="randomised"`, 2026-08-21 survival review): the legacy pooled shift
across all intervals had no likelihood contrast beyond interval 1 and its direction was
prior-mediated; it remains available as the explicit `treatment_window="pooled"` comparator.
A logistic-hazard link is the documented sensitivity variant.
